newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Boots aims to up Italy mkt share.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Boots aims to up Italy mkt share.

text.p: Britain's Boots Company Plc hopes to gain a 20 percent share of Italy's therapeutic skincare market in the medium term through its acquisition of private Italian skin care business Farmila Dermical, Boots Healthcare International (BHI) managing director Barry Clare said.

"That's certainly the challenge," to bring Italian market share to levels in France, where recently acquired Laboratoires Lutsia has sales of around 40 million stg in a market worth 200 million stg, Clare told Reuters in a telephone interview.
He said Farmila Dermical, which Boots bought for 4.1 million stg, has sales of around two million stg in a market worth around 80 million stg.
Boots bought Lutsia for some 115 million stg from Roussel Uclaf in September 1996.
"We don't see any reason why we should not achieve similar levels to France in Italy in the medium term...it is not going to happen overnight," he added.
BHI already sells cold cure and painkiller products in Italy and hopes to add its own-brand E45 skincare range to Lutsia's products to sell in the country, Clare said.
The E45 skincare range has around 60 percent of the UK market but is not as well-known as Lutsia's range in continental Europe.
Clare said first new product launches for Italy could be seen in the spring.
BHI is still looking to buy interests in the German over-the-counter medicines market, he added, along with any fill-in acquisitions or complementary purchases, he said.
"We want to be the leader for therapeutic skincare in Europe," he added, a position that the Boots group already holds in the UK.
"With the Italian purchase, we have got the legs to exploit our product range in Europe," he added.
